items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "Pythagoras' theorem".
items.answer: In a right-angled triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c²

items.stem: Lars says the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with legs 6 cm and 11 cm is 17 cm. Explain why this cannot be right and find the correct length.
items.answer: The sides would not form a triangle (a + b must be longer than c); c = √(36 + 121) = 12.5 cm.
items.markingKey: Reason (triangle inequality or squares not added) (R1); correct method and value (M1 A1).

items.stem: "The hypotenuse of a triangle with legs 5 and 12 is 17." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: You must square, add and then square-root: √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.

A triangle with one angle of exactly 90°
